question: How does funding work for ELEVATES chapters and campus events?
answer: ELEVATES charges zero commercial or franchise fees to the college or students. All core platform infrastructure, playbooks, and community frameworks are free. For campus events and workshops, standard operational funds (such as guest speaker travel allowance/TA, local hospitality, or student project component support) are allocated directly by the college/department or IEDC funds out of heads the institution already holds.

question: Which budget heads do colleges use to fund event operational expenses?
answer: Colleges typically spend from existing heads already collected for this purpose: (1) Department Association Fund collected in published fee structures, (2) IEDC KSUM Activity Budget for KSUM KPIs, (3) PTA Discretionary Fund, or (4) IQAC Quality Initiative Head for NAAC activities. ELEVATES brings the guests, curriculum, and event tooling; the college spends its own budget through its own process.

question: What specifically is required from the college administration?
answer: Four practical things: (1) Seminar hall or computer lab access, (2) One named Faculty Coordinator, (3) Permission to co-brand event announcements, and (4) Standard department or IEDC allocation for guest travel allowance (TA) and student project supplies when organizing major events.

question: How does ELEVATES adapt to different universities in Kerala (KTU, Calicut, MG, Kerala, Kannur, Autonomous)?
answer: Every university has a specific requirement students struggle to complete. For KTU colleges, our project clusters fill Group III Activity Points (startups, patents, shipped projects). For Calicut/MG/Kerala/Kannur Four-Year Programmes (FYUGP 2024), we provide project proof for Skill Enhancement Courses, mandatory internships, and research projects. For Autonomous colleges, we deliver fast-track value-added course modules.

question: How do you handle student data privacy and DPDP Act compliance?
answer: We strictly adhere to India's Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act. Event registration forms include clear consent language. Student data is never sold or shared with commercial third parties. Event photography is conducted only with advance notice.

question: How are guest speakers and event itineraries vetted?
answer: Every guest speaker, workshop topic, and event schedule must be submitted to the designated faculty coordinator for review and clearance prior to the event. Nothing happens on campus without faculty approval.

question: What happens when founding student leaders graduate? Will the chapter collapse?
answer: ELEVATES has a built-in succession framework. Chapter 01 at Eranad Knowledge City successfully handed over full operations to a trained 30-member junior team in August 2026 before the founders graduated. We train new leadership cohorts every academic term.

question: Can non-engineering or arts & science colleges start an ELEVATES Chapter?
answer: Yes. Technology has no department. ELEVATES runs interdisciplinary tracks across Web Development, AI Tools, Digital Marketing, UI/UX Design, and Automation suitable for engineering, polytechnic, and arts & science institutions.
